column1: # Red/green cases for the OSS-Fuzz postgresql harness defects.
# Each case is an assertion about UPSTREAM's harnesses that must FAIL before the
# corresponding fix and PASS after it. Upstream ships no tests for these files,
# so these live here rather than there; they are written against upstream's
# layout so they can be contributed later if the project wants them.
# THE ORACLE IS --enable-cassert. Upstream builds without it (project.yaml lists
# only the address sanitizer), which is precisely why these defects survived for
# years: without assertions a harness that hands the wrong structure to a
# function does not crash, it quietly does the wrong thing. The suite therefore
# builds with assertions on, and that is itself one of the recommendations.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   id       short name, used in output and to pick a single case
#   defect   which defect from FINDINGS/oss-fuzz-harness-bugs it covers
#   needs    defect fixes that must be applied before this case can discriminate,
#            or "-" for none. Defect 13 aborts every backend harness at startup,
#            so cases 1, 2, 3 and 9 cannot observe anything until it is fixed --
#            they are run in a second pass with fixes/13-*.diff applied. 13 itself
#            must therefore run with nothing applied, which is why it is a case
#            and not a precondition. Demoting the most reproducible defect to
#            infrastructure made it invisible in every count.
#   target   fuzz target to run
#   input    file under inputs/, or "-" for none
#   expect   what a FIXED harness does:
#              exit0            runs the input and exits cleanly
#              execs>N          reports more than N executed units
#              wall<N           the run finishes within N seconds. For defects whose
#                               symptom is "nothing stops this" -- no assertion can
#                               express a timeout that never fires, only a clock can.
#              stderr:PATTERN   stderr matches PATTERN (an ERROR, not a crash)
#              covers:FUNC      libFuzzer reports FUNC as covered. The honest form
#                               for a defect whose symptom is "this code is never
#                               reached" rather than a crash -- defect 1 does not
#                               abort, it makes a real statement fail to parse so
#                               everything below is never entered.
#              nocover:FUNC     FUNC must NOT be covered. Defect 2 runs its error
#                               recovery after a successful parse, so recovery
#                               functions appearing on a clean input IS the defect.
#              noassert:PATTERN no `TRAP: failed Assert(...)` matching PATTERN.
#                               This is the discriminating form: matching on exit
#                               status alone counted two unrelated aborts as six
#                               defect reproductions, because an abort is an
#                               abort. A case must name the assertion it expects
#                               to stop firing, or it proves nothing.
#   note     what the defect does when unfixed
# DROPPED: defect 9 (MyBackendType). It needs a temporary relation to actually be
# created, and no deployed target executes statements -- simple_query stops after
# analyse and plan. There is no input to this harness that reaches it, so a case
# would be theatre. The defect is real; it is simply not observable here.
#id
timing-starts
column7: unfixed: pg_initialize_timing() never called, so every backend harness aborts at startup

column1: protocol-starts
column7: unfixed: no dbname in argv, so single-user mode falls back to the username and the backend never boots

column1: json-keeps-context
column7: unfixed: delete_context(TopMemoryContext) while it is current -- a DEPLOYED target

column1: deep-recursion
column7: unfixed: stack base on the init frame, so check_stack_depth never fires

column1: reaches-analyzer
column7: unfixed: parses as a TYPE NAME, so a real statement never reaches the analyser

column1: reaches-planner
column7: unfixed: same cause, one level deeper

column1: no-restart-per-input
column7: unfixed: PostgresSingleUserMain runs again per input, re-entering one-shot startup -- aborts, not asserts

column1: timeout-fires
column7: unfixed: libFuzzer's -timeout cannot fire because PostgreSQL owns the clock

column1: second-error-recovers
column7: unfixed: the fuzzer_first_run guard skips per-call handler setup, so the 2nd error unwinds into a dead frame
